issue:generate.description: Generate ticket descriptions from local files, repo-scoped artifacts via --repos, URLs, or ticket keys. Tracker browse URLs (e.g., https://<org>.atlassian.net/browse/<KEY>) are automatically detected and fetched via the tracker REST API instead of scraping HTML; self-hosted instances are supported when atlassian.baseUrl is configured. Local .md, .json, .yaml, and .yml files that parse as tickets are imported as tickets; files that are not recognized as ticket-formatted content remain plain file sources. Repo-scoped generation inspects prior plan artifacts anywhere under ~/.wf/<repo>/**/* and correlates them by keyword similarity so synthesis prompts can reuse earlier implementation context. When multiple repos are supplied, the synthesis prompt also compares repo conventions, including linter and formatter rules, and git-hook tools across checkouts. AI synthesis always runs on every source to enrich and standardize the output. The AI is instructed to return a structured JSON object (title, type, priority, description) that is validated against the ticket schema before conversion to the requested output format. When agent or CLI backends are used, the provider session ID is threaded across oversized-source summarisation, clarification, and synthesis so all calls share coherent context. Generated output enforces formal writing conventions (concise prose, no contractions, active voice, British English) before display or save. Blank AI generate-stage responses fail fast with provider-aware diagnostics. Can use an agent backend when stages.generate.backend is set to agent

issue:implement.description: Carry out an implementation plan from a ticket-backed, hashed, or custom plan artifact. Delegates the generate-and-verify loop to the configured backend (Anthropic Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, or Claude CLI headless mode) based on stages.implement.provider and stages.implement.backend. Progress events are streamed to the terminal so you can follow task and tool activity while edits are being generated. All backends emit stable task and tool progress lines plus explicit file mutation logs and verification logs so terminal output stays human-readable while the agent works. Verification commands are expected to be repo-root-relative; stale plan artifacts that still embed redundant repo-selection `cd` prefixes are normalized, while cross-repo directory jumps are treated as setup errors. Set stages.implement.provider and stages.implement.backend in wf.config to select the backend. Use backend: agent with provider anthropic or openai for the Agent SDK path, or backend: cli with provider anthropic or openai for the CLI headless mode (Claude CLI or Codex CLI respectively). Set stages.implement.timeoutMs to override the wall-clock subprocess timeout (default: 15 minutes) and stages.implement.inactivityTimeoutMs to override the per-message inactivity timeout (default: 2 minutes). The Anthropic backend explicitly loads ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and the repository-root CLAUDE.md, warning when either file is missing. The OpenAI backend loads ~/.openai/AGENTS.md and the repository-root AGENTS.md with the same warning behavior and only exposes an exact-match verify_command tool for whitelisted verification commands. When running from source, use `yarn start issue:implement ...` for the implementation stage and `yarn start issue:commit -c` to stage the final conventional commit once the work is accepted. Unsupported providers (google, deepseek) fail fast with a clear error listing supported providers. backend: standard is rejected at runtime because the implement stage requires an agent-capable backend. Blank AI findings responses fail fast with provider-aware diagnostics instead of generic parse errors. Repo conventions are detected up front and threaded into every backend prompt, including continuation passes, so formatter and structural ESLint constraints survive context compaction. A complexity-gated commit policy controls whether the backend may self-commit: low-complexity plans block commits so changes remain staged for issue:commit; medium and high plans permit a single commit but rewind any self-made commits via git reset --soft and re-stage the content so issue:commit handles the final message. Enforcement always runs even if the backend throws, and any git safety-check failure (shallow repo, detached HEAD, missing upstream) is logged and treated as a skip rather than an error. Run issue:fetch then issue:plan before calling this command for ticket-backed workflows. When a hashed plan artifact is provided, the action is inferred from the filename/manifest and `--action` becomes optional, but any supplied action is still validated against the resolved artifact. Before implementation, the command runs an interactive branch creation workflow: prompts to create a new branch or stay on the current one, then only checks the working tree for uncommitted changes when a pull is needed. When staying on the current branch, the user is asked whether to pull; stashing is only triggered if a pull is accepted. When creating a new branch, uncommitted changes are stashed before pulling the source branch (dev or main). After each pull, runs a dependency install via the detected package manager (bun, pnpm, yarn, or npm); use --skip-install to suppress. Failures are surfaced as warnings and never abort the command. Generated branch names exceeding 100 characters are automatically truncated at the nearest word boundary. Use --silent to auto-stash without prompting; branch selection and naming still prompt when a TTY is available. Use --no-branch to skip branch creation and work directly on the current branch. Use --branch-name-pattern to override the branch name validation regex from git.branchNamePattern config. When running against multiple repos, repos absent from the plan's affectedRepositories and newRepositories are skipped with a log message. When a plan declares newRepositories, those repos are scaffolded as sibling directories and prepended to the execution order so they run before existing repos. When stages.implement.planStepVerification.enabled is true, a post-implementation AI auditor re-reads the diff and scores each plan step as done, partially-done, not-done, or not-applicable; steps still incomplete trigger an additional fix round in the same session; the loop runs until convergence or stall. stages.implement.planStepVerification.stallWindow (default: 3) sets the sliding-window size for stall detection — the loop exits as stalled when the enriched step content seen in the current round matches any entry in the previous stallWindow rounds. A round whose assessment response is malformed or otherwise fails does not abort the loop — it is retried on the next round, with the actual failure cause recorded in the `step-verify.exhausted` log entry when the stall window is reached; authentication errors (HTTP 401) are the exception and surface immediately as a hard failure. The auditor diffs against the commit HEAD was at before this stage ran (not a possibly-moving HEAD), so committed-but-not-yet-reset work is still visible to the audit even when the commit-policy rewind below is skipped. Verification only runs when the commit policy blocks self-commits (medium/high complexity); low-complexity, stage-and-commit-per-change plans skip it entirely, since their smaller changesets carry less downside risk. When verification is skipped for any reason — config disabled, no working-tree changes, all multi-repo steps are generic (no repo-prefixed path), new-repo run, or commit policy allows direct commit — a `step-verify.skipped reason=<reason>` entry is written to the on-disk agent log so skips are diagnosable rather than silent. In multi-repo mode, generic steps that carry no repo-prefixed file path are excluded from the audit so the assessor only scores actionable steps for the current repo. Steps still pending when rounds are exhausted are listed individually (index, status, and what's missing) in the terminal output and the log, not just as a bare count. Non-auth errors in the verification loop do not abort the wf issue:implement workflow; if no assessor target can be resolved or an unexpected error occurs the loop is skipped and the original result is returned unchanged. Before each verification round, a spec-fidelity pre-pass runs one AI call per assessed step to detect literal claim deviations — regex patterns, required parameters, exact threshold values, and string literals — against the diff. Steps with confirmed concrete mismatches receive a [SPEC FIDELITY ERRORS] annotation that causes the step assessor to score them partially-done and enter a fix round even when the code looks superficially complete. Warning-severity findings (diff is silent on a claim) are surfaced but do not trigger a fix round. The pre-pass is skipped when the diff is empty and never throws; any internal error is silently swallowed so the verification loop is unaffected. Runs a Figma implementation pass when stages.implement.figma is true or --figma is passed; Figma frame links stored in the plan manifest by issue:plan are re-read at implement time to fetch design context via the Figma REST API, injecting frame name, dimensions, and screenshot URL into the backend prompt so the implementer can reconcile generated code against spacing, colour, and component-structure constraints before committing. The manifest is resolved directly from the ticket artifact path so the correct links are always loaded without a branch-name search. Figma frame URLs that lack a `?node-id=` query parameter are skipped with a WARN rather than generating a malformed API call. If all frame fetches fail despite valid links being present, a WARN is written to the on-disk agent log to distinguish network or token failures from the links-absent case.

issue:plan.description: Plan ticket implementation from a local artifact or repo-scoped custom artifact. If a local artifact is not found, the command will attempt to fetch it from the primary tracker. Use --force to fetch and recreate artifacts. Repo-scoped planning inspects prior plan artifacts anywhere under ~/.wf/<repo>/**/* and correlates them by keyword similarity so planning prompts can reuse earlier implementation context. Planning prompts include detected repository test conventions and ecosystem-specific verification guidance so generated steps match local test patterns and only reference allowed command forms. When a design system is detected, observed element class conventions (e.g. h1–h6 heading classes, grid-gap token choices, responsive grid-cols breakpoint tiers mined from real .vue/.tsx files) are included in the plan prompt; the design-system block is omitted for non-UI tickets so the prompt stays focused. Existing components and composables whose names share significant vocabulary with the ticket are surfaced in the plan prompt as reuse candidates so the planner can reference them before creating new files; repos that place UI files outside `app/components` or `app/composables` receive no candidates. Generated plans are semantically validated before they are saved: wf retries once with explicit repair feedback when a draft omits rename targets, uses a non-allowlisted verification command, or contradicts detected test conventions. Targeted verification commands are interpreted as repo-root-relative: redundant `cd <repo>` prefixes are normalized away, while commands that change directories outside the selected repository are rejected. When `--figma` is passed or `stages.plan.figma` is `true`, Figma frame links found in the ticket description or acceptance criteria are extracted with their full query strings (including `?node-id=` parameters) and stored in the plan manifest, enabling Figma REST API design context injection during a later `issue:implement --figma` run and `issue:review --figma` run. When no inline Figma links are found but a design system is detected in the repo, an interactive prompt asks for frame links in TTY sessions; links supplied this way are stored in the manifest but are not threaded into the AI generation context.

issue:review.description: AI-powered code review of local changes, ticket-associated pull requests, or PR diffs. Each review includes nested trace provenance, issue-local suggestions, and diff-aligned inline comment anchors. In multi-repo runs, the review artifact is written to `<ticket>-<repo-basename>-review.md` — one file per repository — so each repo's cached result is stored independently; the first repository's cached review is never served to subsequent repositories in the same run. The review rubric includes Accessibility (roles, focus states, screen-reader operability), Scope & necessity (replaces the former separate Scope and Necessity criteria), and Pattern grounding (checks flagged patterns against actual codebase conventions before raising an issue) among its default criteria. Reviews are enriched with detected repo conventions (linter, formatter, language, TypeScript config) and a verification summary; for PR-backed reviews the verification pipeline (lint, typecheck, test) runs live in a disposable git worktree, leaving the target repository untouched. Use `--skip-verification` to bypass it. Blank or blocked AI review responses fail fast with provider-aware diagnostics instead of generic parse errors. Runs the SonarQube CLI (`sonar analyze secrets` then `sonar analyze`) when `stages.review.sonar` is `true` or `--sonar` is passed; requires `sonar` on PATH and an authenticated `sonar auth status`. Scopes the scan to staged changes when present, otherwise to the merge-base diff against a source branch recovered from `--session-id`, a locally-persisted session for `--ticket-key`, a plan manifest, git reflog, or an interactive prompt, in that order. A bare `--ticket-key` with no matching local session, or any run where no base branch can be resolved, falls back to an unscoped `sonar analyze` and logs a WARN entry to the on-disk log with context `sonar-stage`. Findings are reported and review continues; a clean scan is confirmed too, both on the console and in the persisted log, so it stays distinguishable from a scan that never ran; a missing CLI or auth/project misconfiguration continues the review without Sonar findings, leaving other targets in the same run unaffected. CLI-backed review sessions fork a final human-readable epilogue session so manual provider resume replays readable text instead of raw JSON while the original review session stays intact. Runs a Figma design-conformance check when `stages.review.figma` is `true` or `--figma` is passed; Figma frame links captured from the ticket description during `issue:plan` are stored in the plan manifest and re-read at review time to fetch design context via the Figma REST API, injecting frame name, dimensions, and screenshot URL into the review prompt so the reviewer model can evaluate visual conformance against the original frames. If all frame fetches fail despite valid links being present, a WARN is written to the on-disk agent log to distinguish network or token failures from the links-absent case. When `--ui-design-screenshots` was passed to `issue:plan` or `issue`, the resolved screenshot paths are stored in the plan artifact; at review time those paths are re-read, the images are base64-encoded, and the encoded screenshots are injected into the review prompt as multimodal content so the reviewer can check UI conformance against the original design files. When the review diff exceeds the summarisation threshold (default 80 000 chars), oversized per-file patches are batched into as few CLI calls as possible — grouping files within a 60 000-character chunk budget — rather than one call per file; each batch call returns `=== FILE: <path> ===`-delimited summaries and paths are normalised on both sides to avoid OS separator mismatches. Configure `stages.review.maxDiffLength` (integer ≥ 1) to override the 80 000-character threshold and `stages.review.epilogueTimeoutMs` (integer ≥ 0, default 30 000 ms) to adjust the CLI epilogue spawn timeout. Epilogue failures from `is_error` responses or spawn errors are surfaced in the console log with the first line of the extracted diagnostic so the root cause is visible without opening a log file.
